title: Camp Samac

services.name: Canoe Coaching Clinic
services.desc: Purpose: to introduce Scouters to personal canoeing. This activity will not prepare Scouters for a leadership role in canoeing. Specifically this introductory canoeing activity will not prepare Scouters to take youth on a day or part day of canoeing or on a canoe trip. A recognized, provincially certified canoe course is highly recommended for the above type of activity. Participant Prerequisite: must be able to confidently swim 100m (4 lengths of most municipal pools). There will not be a swim test for this event. Swimming ability must be self-assessed by the participants. Other Items Participants to Provide: snacks, water, brown-bag lunch, coffee/tea, weather-appropriate clothing

services.name: Cabin 1
services.desc: Large galley kitchen, dining hall, small bunk rooms on main floor, 2 sleeping rooms on second floor, 2 sets of washrooms with wheelchair accessibility. Log cabin re-constructed in 1993, ready to host up to 28 people. This cabin is just east of the north parking area. Close to council hall, archery, trail heads and chapel. Heating: natural gas Water: fresh city tap water (hot and cold) Electric lighting and receptacles Accessible ramp and washrooms. Kitchen: refrigerator and freezer, two 4-burner stoves and ovens, triple sink for washing and sanitation. Cleaning supplies, mop and bucket, etc. (No pots, dishes, cutlery.) Washrooms: with flush toilet, toilet

services.name: Campsite Balsam
services.desc: Year round camping is available on level ground. This campsite at the north end of the property and is accessible by walking in from the hydro cut grassed parking area. The area is surprising remote considering there are housing developments surrounding Camp Samac. Access to flush toilet block and city water tap in warm weather, indoor toilet and water in winter can be arranged with the camp
